column36: I DO still wish to participate in the summer school, as a DAY student.
column44:
I took part in the national science olympiad this year and reached the second round. I have read several popular science books, and the chapter on Einstein's theory of relativity was by far my favourite. I watch a lot of lectures online, but I have never had the chance to ask questions to real researchers. For a school project I wrote a short report on Einstein's theory of relativity and I received very positive feedback. During a visit to a science museum I saw a demonstration that made me want to learn much more. Sometimes the subject feels very abstract, and that is exactly the challenge I am looking for. In my free time I build small electronics projects with an Arduino and I like to understand how things work. I also look forward to meeting other students from different countries who share my passion for science.

I am considering studying physics or engineering after secondary school, and this summer school would help me decide. I would be grateful for the opportunity and I promise to make the most of it. My grandfather was an engineer and he always encouraged me to ask why things are the way they are. Living in a student dorm for a week also sounds like a great way to become more independent. I would really like to experience what it is like to study science at a university like KU Leuven. I am a curious person and I am not afraid to work hard on difficult problems. I hope to learn how scientists actually do research, not only the results that end up in textbooks. At school we only scratch the surface of these subjects, so I would love to go deeper during a whole week. Last year my physics teacher showed us a video about Einstein's theory of relativity and I could not stop thinking about it.
